source.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models
source.authors: Naiyu Yin; Dennis Wei; Tian Gao; Amit Dhurandhar; K. Ramamurthy; Yue Yu

record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether pretrained SAE features in an LLM correspond to interpretable concepts using feature activations and targeted prompt changes. This is a different, qualitative test of the SAE-feature part of V4, not a test of toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative SAE-feature examples for GPT-2 small, including measured activations over prompts and prompt changes. Those bear on V4's SAE-feature-recovery component. Its circuit accuracy, runtime, faithfulness/completeness, and downstream debiasing results do not test the claim versions. It does not measure feature overlap, feature directions, sparsity-dependent geometry, or capacity competition.
record.test_reason: This is a circuit-learning method paper (CircuitLasso). It assumes SAE features are monosemantic, citing Bricken et al. and Huben et al., and uses pretrained SAEs as its input. Its results report the method's own performance: SHD and runtime on InterpBench, faithfulness and completeness on CoLA, and debiasing accuracy on Bias-in-Bios. The per-prompt SAE activation tables (Tables 5-8) are not a test of V4. They are hand-picked worked examples of the authors' feature-labelling procedure, applied to features their method ranked highly. There is no baseline, no rate of interpretable features and no comparison against neurons. They show that labelling works for chosen features, not whether a dictionary recovers the model's sparse features.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The central claim is efficiency at parity of accuracy: CircuitLasso matches EAP-ig on circuit recovery at lower cost and scales to SAE feature spaces. The SAE-feature circuits are presented as interpretable and useful for debiasing. The authors limit the propagation patterns to GPT-2 small and leave open whether they hold for more entangled features.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pretrained SAEs and observational feature activations in a circuit-learning method; it does not reproduce the toy-network training or geometric measurements of Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The feature interpretations and circuit paths are based on dataset-level averaged activations or, for per-instance analysis, prompt-specific activation-weighted scores. Results shown here are qualitative and from GPT-2 small.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-layer dependencies among GPT-2 small SAE features show persistence, merging and dropping of concepts (e.g. '-self' across layers 8-12) and spurious co-occurrence links. Shown in hand-chosen traversals (Fig. 3, Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in consecutive layers form sparse linear dependency chains in which concepts persist, merge or drop.

record.problems: The feature interpretation is qualitative and manually labelled, uses a selected GPT-2 small model and SAE dictionary, and does not establish feature completeness, stability, canonical status, or generality. The authors also note that their learned dependencies can include spurious correlations.
record.rows_left_out: Circuit-learning benchmark comparisons, CoLA faithfulness/completeness ablations, and Bias-in-Bios performance results were left out because they measure the proposed circuit method or downstream debiasing, not whether the claim's representation properties hold.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or feature geometry.
No capacity or importance analysis of polysemanticity.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity examined.
No measure of features spread across neurons, and no systematic rate of SAE features recovering sparse structure. Only illustrative examples of selected features.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The paper takes SAE monosemanticity as a premise. The activation tables are worked examples of its labelling procedure for features selected by its own regression coefficients, with no baseline or population rate. So they cannot support or limit V4. The reader's limits_scope label was based on a generality caveat, which is an untested part, not a qualification.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, excess sparse features relative to dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, and sparsity-dependent transitions or geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.

The paper gives qualitative evidence for SAE features corresponding to interpretable concepts in GPT-2 small, but does not test whether features are distributed across many neurons. It does not establish generality across models or compare against a ground-truth feature dictionary.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features as the model's representational units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multi-dimensional.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected SAE features in GPT-2 small on the reported prompts
reader_labels.reason: The authors identify interpretable concepts from SAE-feature activations across prompts and show targeted input changes that alter the corresponding feature activations (R1-R24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The qualitative interpretability examples in this study
reader_labels.reason: The evidence is a hand-interpreted case study of GPT-2 small and its SAE dictionary; the authors explicitly do not claim that the observations transfer unchanged to larger or more modern models (R1-R24).
